For cyclic \(B,O,X,C\), angles subtending chord \(BC\) are equal: \(\angle BXC=\angle BOC=2n\). Now \(BX\) bisects \(\angle B\), so \(\angle XBC=B/2\). Also \(CX\) is perpendicular to \(AB\), hence \(\angle XCB=90^\circ-B\). Therefore \(\angle BXC=180^\circ-B/2-(90^\circ-B)=90^\circ+B/2\). Thus \(2n=90^\circ+B/2\), so \(B=4n-180\). Angle sum gives \(C=180-n-B=360-5n\). The acute conditions give \(n<90\), \(B<90\Rightarrow n<67.5\), \(C<90\Rightarrow n>54\), plus \(B>0\Rightarrow n>45\) and \(C>0\Rightarrow n<72\). Hence \(54<n<67.5\). The largest integer is \(67\), and it works: \(A=67,B=88,C=25\) are all acute. Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{67}\).
